name: SafeWaze Shock-Absorbing Lanyard
title: SafeWaze Shock-Absorbing Lanyard for Aerial Lifts
meta: A SafeWaze shock absorbing lanyard for bucket trucks and aerial lifts. How it ties you to the boom anchor, what the pack does, and how to inspect it before work.
tagline: A shock-absorbing fall arrest lanyard for bucket truck and aerial lift operators.
summary: The SafeWaze shock absorbing lanyard connects your full-body harness to the anchor point in a bucket truck or aerial lift. If you are thrown from the platform, the energy-absorbing pack deploys and limits the force that reaches your body.
highlights: Built for full-body harness use in aerial lifts
Locking snap hooks at each end
Webbing lanyard that stays out of the way in the bucket
Labels carry the ratings and the inspection record

body.h: Why the bucket needs a lanyard
p: A bucket truck feels solid until the boom gets bumped by a falling limb, a rope loads unexpectedly, or the truck shifts on soft ground. A short catapult is all it takes to throw an operator out of the bucket. A shock-absorbing lanyard clipped to the manufacturer's anchor point keeps you with the machine.

Clip to the anchor on the boom or platform, not to the bucket lip or a hydraulic line, and keep the lanyard as short as your work allows. Browse our fall arrest gear for aerial lifts for harnesses and other lanyards.

Check the lanyard before every shift. Look at the webbing for cuts, burns, chemical damage, and stiff or glazed spots. Make sure the shock pack cover is intact and has not started to deploy, and that each snap hook opens, closes, and locks cleanly.

Any lanyard that has arrested a fall comes out of service for good. Follow the SafeWaze instructions, your employer's fall protection program, and ANSI Z133 for work in aerial devices, and make sure everyone in the bucket is trained on the gear they wear.

faq.q: Can I use a shock-absorbing lanyard for tree climbing?
faq.a: No. It is fall arrest gear for aerial lifts and other anchored work positions. Climbing a tree takes a climbing line and lanyard system built and rated for that job.

faq.q: What do I do after the lanyard catches a fall?
faq.a: Take it out of service and replace it, even if it looks fine. The shock pack is designed to work once.

name: Husqvarna X-Tough Chainsaw Bar 3/8" .050"
title: Husqvarna X-Tough Bar 3/8" .050": Fit and Buying Guide
meta: The Husqvarna X-Tough bar in 3/8 pitch and .050 gauge is a solid pro bar for big saws and hard felling. How to match length, chain, and mount before you buy.
tagline: A solid, heavy-duty Husqvarna bar for 3/8" .050" chain on pro saws.
summary: The Husqvarna X-Tough bar is a solid steel guide bar for professional saws running 3/8" pitch, .050" gauge chain. It is built for removals, big-wood bucking, and felling where a lighter laminated bar would flex or wear out too soon.
highlights: Solid bar body for heavy, hard use
Several lengths for different saw sizes

body.h: When to step up to a solid bar
p: Laminated bars are light and fine for most climbing and limbing work. On the ground saw that bucks big logs all day, though, a solid bar like the X-Tough holds its rails longer, shrugs off pinches better, and can be dressed and turned many times before it is done.
It adds weight, so it makes the most sense on a 70 cc and larger saw where balance already favors a longer bar. Compare lengths and mounts in our chainsaw bars.

Three things have to match: the mount on your saw, the 3/8" pitch and .050" gauge of the chain, and the drive link count for the length you choose. Check your saw's manual or the old bar's stamping before ordering. A bar that fits the studs but not the oiler hole will run dry and wear fast.

Flip the bar each time you change the chain, file burrs off the rails, keep the oil hole and groove clean, and grease the nose sprocket. Always run a sharp, properly tensioned chain and wear chainsaw protective gear.

faq.q: Will the X-Tough bar fit my saw?
faq.a: It depends on the mount and length. Match the bar mount to your saw model and confirm the chain is 3/8" pitch, .050" gauge with the right drive link count.

faq.q: Is a solid bar worth it for climbing saws?
faq.a: Usually not. Solid bars are heavier and pay off on large ground saws used for felling and bucking.

name: Clogger Ascend Gen 2 Chainsaw Pants
title: Clogger Ascend Gen 2 Chainsaw Pants for Climbing Arborists
meta: Clogger Ascend Gen 2 chainsaw pants are light, stretchy protective trousers for climbers. What they protect, how they fit in a saddle, and how to care for them.
tagline: Lightweight, stretchy chainsaw pants cut for climbing arborists.
summary: The Clogger Ascend Gen 2 chainsaw pants are lightweight protective trousers designed around tree climbing. They put cut-resistant layers on the front of the legs in a stretch shell that moves when you are stepping high, kneeling on a limb, or working in a saddle all day.
highlights: Stretch panels for high steps and limb walks
Cut-resistant protective layers in the legs
Light enough for full days in the tree
Cut to work with a saddle and leg loops
specs: Tree climbing and general saw work
See the label on the garment

p: Most chainsaw pants were designed for loggers on the ground. The Ascend line was built for climbers, so the fabric stretches where you bend, the protection stays where a saw is most likely to touch you, and the cut is slim enough to sit under leg loops without bunching.
That matters on a hot day halfway through a removal. Pants that move with you and breathe are pants you actually keep on. See our other chainsaw pants for more options.

body.h: What the protection does and doesn't do
p: Cut-resistant layers work by pulling fibers into the chain and stopping the sprocket. They reduce injury, they do not make you saw-proof, and they only cover the protected zones. Good saw handling, a sharp chain, and training still come first, in line with ANSI Z133.
Wash them by the label instructions, keep them away from bar oil buildup and heat, and retire any pair that has been cut into the protective layer.

faq.q: Can I patch Clogger pants after a saw cut?
faq.a: No. Once the protective layer has been cut, the pants should be replaced. A patch on the shell does not restore the protection.

faq.q: Do they fit under a climbing saddle?
faq.a: Yes. The Ascend pants are cut for climbers and are meant to be worn with a saddle and leg loops.

name: Clogger Ember Chainsaw Pants
title: Clogger Ember Chainsaw Pants: Fit, Use and Care
meta: Clogger Ember chainsaw pants give arborists and saw operators leg protection in a trouser they can wear all day. Fit, care, and when to replace them explained.
tagline: Protective chainsaw trousers from Clogger for day-in, day-out saw work.
summary: Clogger Ember chainsaw pants are protective trousers for arborists and saw operators who want leg protection built into a pant rather than strapped on as chaps. They are meant to be worn all day, on the ground or in the tree.
highlights: Cut-resistant layers in the front of the legs
Trouser fit instead of strap-on chaps
Suited to ground and climbing work
From Clogger, a specialist in saw protective wear
Easy to wear with a saddle or tool belt
specs: See the label on the garment

p: Chaps are quick to put on over jeans and easy to share across a crew. Pants like the Ember stay put, do not flap when you climb or drag brush, and do not have straps to snag. If you run a saw most of the day, pants are often the more comfortable choice.
Check the size chart and try them with your boots and saddle before a long day. Compare other styles in our chainsaw pants section.
Wash protective pants as the label directs. Oil and sawdust buildup can affect how the protective fibers work, so keep them reasonably clean. Avoid patching or altering the legs.

Any cut that reaches the protective layer means the pants are done. Remember they reduce injury from a running chain but do not prevent it. Training, a sharp chain, and safe saw handling under ANSI Z133 do most of the work.

faq.q: Are chainsaw pants better than chaps?
faq.a: Neither is safer by default. Pants are more comfortable for all-day and climbing work; chaps are quicker to put on and share.

faq.q: How do I know what standard they meet?
faq.a: Read the label sewn into the pants. It lists the standard and the protection class.

name: Eagle 5 Gallon Yellow Safety Can
title: Eagle 5 Gallon Yellow Safety Can for Diesel Fuel
meta: The Eagle 5 gallon safety can in yellow is the standard color for diesel. Galvanized steel, self-closing lid, flame arrester. Why it beats a plastic jug on the truck.
tagline: A galvanized steel 5 gallon safety can in yellow, the color crews use for diesel.
summary: The Eagle 5 gallon safety can is a galvanized steel fuel can with a spring-closing lid and a flame arrester in the spout. Yellow is the common color for diesel, which helps keep chipper and truck fuel from ending up in a saw.
highlights: Yellow marks the can for diesel

p: A steel safety can vents pressure through its lid instead of swelling and splitting, and the flame arrester screen helps keep an outside flame from reaching the fuel inside. It holds up to being tossed in a truck bed far better than a plastic jug.
Color coding is simple insurance. Red for gas, yellow for diesel, and a different can for mixed saw fuel keeps a tired crew from fueling the wrong machine. See our other fuel cans and fluids.

Strap the can upright in the truck, keep it out of the cab, and fill it on the ground rather than in a bed liner, so static can bleed off. Let engines cool before fueling, and keep the area clear of running saws and smoking.
Inspect the lid seal and spring, and replace a can that is dented at the seams or leaking. A replacement funnel makes pouring into a chipper or skid steer tank cleaner.

faq.q: Can I put gasoline in a yellow can?
faq.a: It will hold it, but yellow is the common color for diesel. Use a red can for gasoline so nobody mixes them up.

faq.q: Does it come with a funnel?
faq.a: A funnel can be added to Eagle safety cans for pouring into small openings. We list a replacement funnel separately.

name: Eagle Safety Can Replacement Funnel
title: Eagle Safety Can Replacement Funnel
meta: An Eagle safety can replacement funnel for pouring fuel into saws, chippers, and equipment without spills. What it fits and how to keep it clean and working.
tagline: A replacement pour funnel for Eagle steel safety cans.
summary: The Eagle safety can funnel attaches to the spout of an Eagle safety can so you can pour into a narrow fuel opening without spilling. It is a simple replacement when the old funnel is lost, bent, or cracked.
highlights: Cuts down on spills around hot engines
Quick to swap on the job
specs: Eagle safety cans (check your can model)

body.h: A small part that saves fuel
p: Pouring from a 5 gallon can straight into a chipper or loader tank is a good way to splash fuel on a warm engine. The funnel puts the stream where it belongs, and that means less waste, less mess in the truck, and less fire risk.
Check that the funnel matches your Eagle can before ordering, since cans differ by model. You can find matching cans in our fluids section.
Wipe the funnel after use and store it so dirt and sawdust do not get carried into the next tank. Grit in fuel is hard on carburetors and injectors.
Replace a funnel that is cracked or no longer seats firmly, and fuel only with the engine off and cooled.

faq.q: Will it fit any brand of safety can?
faq.a: It is made for Eagle cans. Check your can's model before buying.

faq.q: Can I use it for bar oil?
faq.a: Keep a separate funnel for oil so you don't contaminate fuel. Use this one for the fuel the can holds.

name: Chipper Knife 7-1/4" x 4-1/2" x 1/2"
title: Chipper Knife 7-1/4 x 4-1/2 x 1/2: Fit and Care
meta: A 7-1/4 x 4-1/2 x 1/2 chipper knife for brush chippers. How to confirm the fit, when to sharpen or replace, and how to change knives safely on a disc or drum.
tagline: A replacement brush chipper knife, 7-1/4 in long, 4-1/2 in wide, 1/2 in thick.
summary: This 7-1/4 x 4-1/2 x 1/2 chipper knife is a replacement blade for brush chippers that take a knife of that size. Sharp knives pull brush in faster, make cleaner chips, and put less strain on the engine and the feed system.
highlights: 7-1/4 in long, 4-1/2 in wide, 1/2 in thick
Replace in matched sets for balance

p: Size is only part of the match. Bolt hole count, spacing, and the bevel angle also have to fit your chipper. Compare against your machine manual or an old knife before ordering. Other sizes are in our chipper knives section.
Change knives as a set so the disc or drum stays balanced, and keep the old ones for regrinding.

Shut the chipper down, remove the key, and wait for the disc or drum to stop completely. Lock it out the way the manufacturer specifies before reaching in. Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling knives.
Torque the bolts to spec, use new hardware when the manual calls for it, and check the anvil gap after a knife change. Dull knives make the chipper work harder and throw more long stringy material.

faq.q: Will this knife fit my chipper?
faq.a: Only if your chipper uses a 7-1/4 x 4-1/2 x 1/2 knife with the same bolt pattern. Check the manual or an old knife.

faq.q: Can I sharpen chipper knives?
faq.a: Yes, within the minimum width the chipper maker allows. Grind cool and keep the original angle.

name: Chipper Knife 7-1/4" x 4" x 1/2"
title: Chipper Knife 7-1/4 x 4 x 1/2: Replacement Blade
meta: A 7-1/4 x 4 x 1/2 chipper knife for brush chippers. Check the bolt pattern before ordering, sharpen or swap in sets, and lock out the machine before changing.
tagline: A replacement brush chipper knife, 7-1/4 in long, 4 in wide, 1/2 in thick.
summary: This 7-1/4 x 4 x 1/2 chipper knife is a replacement blade for brush chippers built around that knife size. A fresh edge keeps the feed rollers pulling, the chips small, and fuel use down.
highlights: 7-1/4 in long, 4 in wide, 1/2 in thick
For brush chippers that use this size

body.h: Signs it's time for new knives
p: When the chipper starts bogging on brush it used to eat, the feed rollers hesitate, or the chips come out long and shredded, the knives are usually dull or chipped. Rocks, nails, and dirt in the brush pile speed that up.
Before ordering, check the bolt hole pattern and bevel against your manual or an old knife. The 4 in width is easy to confuse with the 4-1/2 in version. See the rest of our chipper knives.
Turn the machine off, take the key, and wait for full stop before opening the hood. Lock the disc or drum as the manufacturer describes, and wear cut-resistant gloves.
Replace knives in sets, torque the bolts to spec, and reset the anvil clearance. Keep a spare set in the truck so a hidden nail doesn't end the day.

faq.q: Is 7-1/4 x 4 interchangeable with 7-1/4 x 4-1/2?
faq.a: No. The width is different, so check which one your chipper takes.

faq.q: How often should I sharpen?
faq.a: It depends on what you feed it. Dirty brush and roots dull knives much faster than clean limbs.

name: Spencer Logging Tape 35' Refill
title: Spencer Logging Tape 35 ft Refill
meta: A Spencer logging tape 35 ft refill for the logger's tape on your belt. Swap in a fresh blade when the old one is kinked or worn, and keep measuring log lengths.
tagline: A 35 ft replacement blade for a Spencer logger's tape.
summary: This Spencer logging tape refill is a 35 ft replacement blade for a Spencer logger's tape. When the old tape is kinked, torn, or worn unreadable, a refill gets your case back in service without buying a whole new tape.
highlights: Fits Spencer logger's tape cases of matching size
Hook end for pinning to the log
Cheaper than replacing the whole tape

body.h: Why crews keep a logger's tape
p: A logger's tape rides on the belt, hooks the end of a log, and rewinds on its own, so you can mark cut lengths for firewood, sawlogs, or a customer's chosen length without walking back to the truck. Spencer tapes are a long-time favorite for that job.
Blades take a beating from sawdust, sap, and getting stepped on. A refill is the fix. See other measuring and cruising tools in our forestry tools.
Check that the refill matches your case model and length before you order. Follow Spencer's instructions to unwind the old blade and wind in the new one, and keep fingers clear of the spring.
Wipe sap off the blade now and then and let it rewind under control so the hook doesn't snap back.

faq.q: Will a 35 ft refill fit any Spencer case?
faq.a: It needs to match your case model. Check the case before ordering.

faq.q: Can I replace just the hook?
faq.a: Usually the hook comes with the refill blade. Replacing the whole blade is the simple fix.

name: Husqvarna 12" Timber Tongs
title: Husqvarna 12" Timber Tongs for Moving Logs
meta: Husqvarna timber tongs with a 12 inch opening let you grab and drag logs and rounds without bending over. How crews use them and how to keep the points sharp.
tagline: Steel log tongs for grabbing and dragging rounds and short logs.
summary: Husqvarna timber tongs grab a log or round with two pointed jaws so you can drag or lift it with a straight back. The 12 inch size suits firewood rounds, brush stems, and short logs on cleanup.
highlights: Jaws bite harder as you pull
Keeps hands away from the log and the saw

p: Cleanup after a removal is mostly lifting and dragging. Tongs let you hook a round, pull it to the pile or the trailer, and keep your fingers out from under it. With two people on a pair each, you can carry a heavier piece between you.
The 12 inch size is handy for rounds and stems you would otherwise grab by hand. For rolling bigger wood, look at a peavey in our log handling tools.
Set the points into solid wood, not bark that can shear off, and pull straight. The jaws tighten as you pull, so a firm set holds well.
Keep the points sharp with a file and check the pivot for wear. Stay clear of the saw operator and watch your footing on slash.

faq.q: Can two people carry a log with tongs?
faq.a: Yes. Each person uses a pair and lifts together. Keep it within what you can both handle safely.

faq.q: What size tongs do I need?
faq.a: Match the jaw opening to the diameter you move most. A 12 in pair suits firewood rounds and smaller logs.

name: LogRite Aluminum Handled Peavey
title: LogRite Aluminum Handled Peavey: Roll Big Logs
meta: The LogRite peavey has a light aluminum handle and a steel hook and spike for rolling logs. How it compares with a cant hook and how to pick the right length.
tagline: A light, strong aluminum-handled peavey for rolling and positioning logs.
summary: The LogRite peavey pairs a lightweight aluminum handle with a steel hook and a pointed spike, giving you leverage to roll, turn, and pry logs on the ground. Crews use it to free pinched bars, turn logs for bucking, and stack wood at the landing.
highlights: Spike tip for prying and pushing
Made in the USA by LogRite

p: A cant hook has a short toe on the end, while a peavey has a pointed spike. The spike lets you push, pry, and pivot logs and still works for rolling. For general tree work and bucking, many climbers and groundies prefer the peavey for that reason.
Longer handles give more leverage on big logs; shorter ones are easier in tight yards. See our log handling tools for other options.

Set the hook firmly, stand uphill of the log, and keep your feet out of its path. Never stand on the downhill side of a log you are rolling. Roll a pinched log to open the kerf instead of yanking the saw.
Check the hook and its bolt before use and keep the hook point sharp so it bites into bark.

faq.q: Why aluminum instead of wood?
faq.a: Aluminum is light and does not crack or rot like a wooden handle can, and LogRite designs it to take hard use.

faq.q: What length should I buy?
faq.a: Pick by the log diameter you move most. Longer handles give more leverage on large wood.

name: Husqvarna 535i XP Battery Chainsaw 14"
title: Husqvarna 535i XP 14" Battery Chainsaw Review and Specs
meta: The Husqvarna 535i XP is a light 36V battery chainsaw with a 14 inch bar for limbing, pruning, and storm cleanup. Specs, battery notes, and where it fits on a crew.
tagline: A light rear-handle 36V battery saw with a 14 in bar for ground and cleanup work.
summary: The Husqvarna 535i XP is a 36V rear-handle battery chainsaw that runs a 14 inch bar and weighs about 5.7 lb without the battery. It suits limbing, light bucking, pruning cuts from the ground, and work where noise and fumes matter.
highlights: Rear-handle saw with a 14 in bar
Light enough for one-handed carrying between cuts
Quiet, no fuel mixing or pull starting
Shares batteries with other Husqvarna 36V tools

p: On residential jobs, school grounds, and early starts, a battery saw is easy on neighbors. The 535i XP starts on the trigger, runs without exhaust, and makes quick work of limbing and small cleanup cuts. It pairs well with a top-handle battery saw for the climber.
It is not a replacement for a 60 cc gas saw on big wood. Think of it as the groundie's limbing saw. See other battery powered equipment that shares the same battery.
Runtime depends on the battery size and the wood. Many crews carry two batteries and swap while one charges in the truck. Keep batteries out of extreme heat and cold.

Keep the chain sharp and tensioned and the oil reservoir full. Even quiet saws kick back. Wear chainsaw protective pants or chaps, eye and hearing protection, and follow ANSI Z133 and the operator's manual.

faq.q: Is the 535i XP a top-handle saw?
faq.a: No. It is a rear-handle saw. For in-tree work, Husqvarna makes the T535i XP top-handle version.

faq.q: Does it come with a battery?
faq.a: It is often sold as a bare tool. Check the listing for what's included.

name: Air Filter Assembly for Husqvarna 372XP
title: Husqvarna 372XP Air Filter Assembly
meta: A replacement Husqvarna 372XP air filter assembly to keep dust out of the engine. When to clean or replace it, and how a clogged filter robs a big saw of power.
tagline: A replacement air filter assembly for the Husqvarna 372XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 372XP air filter assembly replaces a worn, torn, or clogged filter on one of the most common pro saws on tree crews. A clean filter keeps grit out of the cylinder and lets the saw make full power.
highlights: Keeps dust and chips out of the engine

p: A 372XP spends its life in sawdust. A dirty filter starves the engine of air so it runs rich, loses power, and fouls plugs. A torn filter is worse: fine dust gets through and scores the piston and cylinder.
Check the filter at every refuel on dusty jobs. Find more replacement parts in our power equipment parts.
Tap or brush off loose dust and clean the filter as Husqvarna describes. Do not blow compressed air through it from the outside, which drives dust deeper.
Replace it when it is torn, will not come clean, or no longer seals. Always confirm the part against your saw's model and serial number.

faq.q: Does this fit the 372XP X-Torque?
faq.a: Check the part listing against your exact model and serial number. Some filters differ between versions.

faq.q: How often should I replace it?
faq.a: When it is damaged or won't clean up. On dusty work, check it every tank.

name: Air Filter Cover for Echo CS-2511T
title: Echo CS-2511T Air Filter Cover Replacement
h1: Air Filter Cover for Echo CS-2511T
meta: A replacement Echo CS-2511T air filter cover for the popular small top-handle saw. Keeps chips off the filter and the latch secure. Check fit and install notes.
tagline: A replacement air filter cover for the Echo CS-2511T top-handle saw.
summary: This Echo CS-2511T air filter cover replaces a cracked, lost, or worn cover on Echo's small top-handle saw. The cover keeps chips and dust away from the air filter and holds it in place on the climb.
highlights: Protects the air filter from chips
Restores a secure fit after a lost or broken cover

p: The CS-2511T is a favorite climbing saw because it is light and easy to handle on a lanyard. That also means it gets bumped against limbs and dropped into the bed of the truck, and the filter cover takes the hits. A cracked cover lets chips pack around the filter and can come off in the tree.
Find other parts in our power equipment parts section.
Confirm the part against your saw's model and, if Echo lists it, the serial range. Make sure the filter is clean and seated before closing the cover, and check that it latches firmly.
Top-handle saws are for trained arborists working in trees. Follow the operator's manual and ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Will it fit the CS-2511P?
faq.a: Check the parts listing. Covers can differ between models, so match it to your exact saw.

faq.q: Is the filter included?
faq.a: No. This is the cover only.

name: Air Filter Felt for Husqvarna 395XP
title: Husqvarna 395XP Air Filter Felt Replacement
meta: A replacement Husqvarna 395XP air filter felt to keep fine dust out of a big-bore saw. How to check it, clean it, and when to replace it on hard-working felling saws.
tagline: A replacement filter felt for the Husqvarna 395XP air filter.
summary: This Husqvarna 395XP air filter felt is a replacement filter element for one of the biggest saws a tree crew runs. The 395XP pulls a lot of air, and a clean, intact felt keeps fine dust out of the cylinder.
highlights: Catches fine dust before it reaches the engine
Restores power lost to a clogged filter
Cheap protection for an expensive saw

p: A 395XP is usually the felling and bucking saw for the biggest wood on the job. It works hard and makes a lot of chips. A plugged felt robs it of power and a torn one lets dust wear the piston and rings. Both are cheap to fix compared with a top end.
Find more 395XP and other parts in our power equipment parts.
Look at the felt every tank on dusty work. Clean it as Husqvarna recommends, and replace it if it is torn, matted with oil, or no longer seals.
Make sure the felt sits right in the filter housing before you close the cover so air cannot bypass it.

faq.q: Can I wash the felt?
faq.a: Follow Husqvarna's cleaning instructions for your filter. Replace it if it's torn or won't come clean.

faq.q: How do I know it's the right part?
faq.a: Match it to your saw's model and serial number in the Husqvarna parts listing.

name: Cylinder Base Gasket for Husqvarna 550XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II Cylinder Base Gasket
h1: Cylinder Base Gasket for Husqvarna 550XP Mark II
meta: A cylinder base gasket for the Husqvarna 550XP Mark II. Seals the cylinder to the crankcase so the saw holds compression. Use a new one at every top-end job.
tagline: A cylinder base gasket for the Husqvarna 550XP Mark II.
summary: This Husqvarna 550XP Mark II base gasket seals the cylinder to the crankcase. Any time the cylinder comes off for a piston, ring, or top-end job, a new base gasket goes back on.
highlights: Prevents air leaks and lean running
Use a new gasket every time the cylinder comes off

p: A two-stroke engine depends on a sealed crankcase. If the base gasket leaks, the saw pulls in extra air, runs lean, and can seize. Gaskets compress once and should not be reused, even if they look fine.
Order it with the rest of your top-end parts. See our power equipment parts for more 550XP parts.
Clean both mating surfaces without gouging them, and set the gasket dry unless the service manual says otherwise. Torque cylinder bolts to spec in the correct pattern.
After a top-end job, a pressure and vacuum test is the best way to confirm the seal before the saw goes back to work.

faq.q: Is the base gasket the same as the cylinder gasket?
faq.a: Listings often use both names for the gasket between cylinder and crankcase. Check the part number against your saw.

faq.q: Can I reuse the old gasket?
faq.a: No. Always fit a new one when the cylinder is removed.

name: Clutch Assembly for Husqvarna 390XP
title: Husqvarna 390XP Clutch Assembly Replacement
meta: A replacement Husqvarna 390XP clutch assembly for a big saw that slips, drags the chain at idle, or won't engage. Signs of wear and what to replace at the same time.
tagline: A replacement clutch assembly for the Husqvarna 390XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 390XP clutch assembly replaces a worn or broken clutch on Husqvarna's big-bore felling saw. A healthy clutch engages cleanly under throttle and lets the chain stop at idle.
highlights: Fixes slipping or a chain that creeps at idle
Fit with a new drum or rim sprocket if worn

p: A clutch that slips smells hot, glazes the drum, and loses power in the cut. Broken springs or worn shoes can also leave the chain turning at idle, which is a hazard. If the chain moves at idle after adjusting the carburetor, inspect the clutch.
Find matching drums, sprockets, and other parts in our power equipment parts.
Remove the spark plug lead, lock the piston with a proper piston stop, and use the right clutch tool. Note the thread direction in the service manual.
Check the clutch drum, rim sprocket, and needle bearing while it is apart and replace worn parts. Grease the bearing, and test that the chain stops at idle before going back to work.

faq.q: Should I replace the drum too?
faq.a: If the drum is grooved, glazed, or the sprocket is worn, yes. A new clutch on a worn drum wears out faster.

faq.q: Why is my chain turning at idle?
faq.a: Idle speed set too high or a worn clutch spring are common causes. Check both.

name: Cylinder Gasket for Husqvarna 550XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II Cylinder Gasket
h1: Cylinder Gasket for Husqvarna 550XP Mark II
meta: A cylinder gasket for the Husqvarna 550XP Mark II. Keep a fresh one on hand for top-end rebuilds so the saw seals, holds compression, and doesn't run lean.
tagline: A replacement cylinder gasket for the Husqvarna 550XP Mark II.
summary: This Husqvarna 550XP Mark II cylinder gasket is a new seal for when the cylinder comes off for a piston, rings, or a cleanup after a lean seize. The 550XP Mark II is a common ground saw on tree crews, and gaskets are worth keeping in the parts bin.

p: Scored piston, broken ring, or a cylinder pulled to check for damage: each one means a new gasket. The old gasket has already been compressed and will not seal again reliably.
Order the gasket with any other top-end parts so the saw is not down twice. See our power equipment parts for the rest.
Clean the surfaces carefully, follow the bolt torque and pattern in the service manual, and pressure and vacuum test the engine if you can.
An air leak after a rebuild makes the saw run lean and hot. Fix the cause of the original failure, often a dirty filter or an air leak, before running it hard.

faq.q: Is this different from the base gasket?
faq.a: Names vary between sellers. Check the Husqvarna part number for your saw.

faq.q: Do I need sealant?
faq.a: Follow the service manual. Most cylinder gaskets go in dry.

name: Husqvarna Anti-Vibration Spring for 395XP
title: Husqvarna 395XP Anti-Vibration Spring
meta: A replacement Husqvarna 395XP anti vibration spring. A broken AV spring makes the saw rattle and wears your hands. Signs of failure and how to check the mounts.
tagline: A replacement anti-vibration spring for the Husqvarna 395XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 395XP anti vibration spring replaces a broken or tired spring between the handle and the engine. The AV system is what makes running a big saw for hours bearable on your hands and arms.
highlights: Easy to replace with basic tools

p: A 395XP is a heavy, high-torque saw. Its anti-vibration springs separate the engine from the handles. When one breaks, the saw feels loose, the handle rattles, and more vibration goes into your hands. Over time that contributes to numbness and hand problems.
Check the other springs and mounts at the same time. Find them in our power equipment parts.
With the saw off and cool, grip the handle and the engine and feel for slop. Look for cracked, stretched, or missing springs and worn mounts.
Confirm which position your spring sits in, since a saw can use more than one type. Install washers and plugs as the parts diagram shows.

faq.q: How do I know an AV spring is broken?
faq.a: The handle feels loose or clunks against the engine, and vibration increases. Inspect each mount.

faq.q: Are all the 395XP springs the same?
faq.a: Not always. Check the parts diagram for the position you are replacing.

name: Husqvarna Chainsaw Maintenance Kit for 545 and 550XP
title: Husqvarna 545 and 550XP Chainsaw Maintenance Kit
h1: Husqvarna Chainsaw Maintenance Kit for 545 and 550XP
meta: A Husqvarna 550XP maintenance kit for the 545 and 550XP. Basic wear parts in one box so a seasonal service is quick. What to check while the saw is apart.
tagline: A service kit with common wear parts for the Husqvarna 545 and 550XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 550XP maintenance kit bundles common wear parts for the 545 and 550XP so you can service the saw in one sitting. It is an easy way to keep a working saw running strong through the season.
highlights: Common wear parts in one kit
Good to keep in the shop for each saw

p: Kits like this typically cover the parts that wear from normal use, such as the air filter, spark plug, and fuel filter. Check the listing for the exact contents. Swapping them on a schedule prevents most hard-starting and low-power complaints.
The 545 and 550XP are workhorse ground saws for many crews, so a kit per saw at the start of the season makes sense. See more parts in our power equipment parts.

Clean the cooling fins and flywheel, check the clutch, drum, and sprocket, inspect the bar and oiler, and look over the AV mounts and chain brake. Test the chain brake before the saw goes back to work.
Use fresh fuel mixed to Husqvarna's ratio or a pre-mixed fuel. Most running problems start with old fuel or a dirty filter.

faq.q: What's in the kit?
faq.a: Contents vary by kit version. Check the listing; most include filters and a spark plug.

faq.q: How often should I service my saw?
faq.a: Follow Husqvarna's schedule, and service more often on dusty, full-time work.

name: Husqvarna Clutch Assembly for 372XP X-Torque
title: Husqvarna 372XP X-Torque Clutch Assembly
meta: A replacement Husqvarna 372XP clutch assembly for the X-Torque model. Fixes slipping, grabbing, or a chain that creeps at idle. How to check and replace it.
tagline: A replacement clutch assembly for the Husqvarna 372XP X-Torque.
summary: This Husqvarna 372XP clutch assembly is a replacement for the X-Torque version of the 372XP, a go-to 70 cc class saw on tree crews. A good clutch grabs the chain smoothly under throttle and releases it at idle.
highlights: Fixes a creeping chain at idle
Check drum and sprocket while it's apart

p: Slipping in the cut, a burning smell, a blue or glazed drum, or a chain that turns at idle all point toward the clutch. Rule out a high idle setting first, then pull the clutch and look for broken springs or worn shoes.
Make sure you order the X-Torque version if that is your saw. More parts are in our power equipment parts.
Disconnect the plug, use a piston stop, and use the correct clutch tool. The clutch threads are reverse on many saws, so check the service manual.
Inspect and replace the drum, rim sprocket, and needle bearing if worn, grease the bearing, and confirm the chain stops at idle after reassembly.

faq.q: Will this fit an older 372XP?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Match it to your exact model and serial number.

faq.q: Why replace the sprocket at the same time?
faq.a: A worn rim sprocket eats chains and loads the clutch unevenly.

name: Husqvarna Cylinder Gasket for 395XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 395XP Cylinder Gasket Replacement
meta: A Husqvarna 395XP cylinder gasket for top-end service on the big felling saw. Fit a new gasket every time the cylinder comes off to keep the engine sealed.
tagline: A replacement cylinder gasket for the Husqvarna 395XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 395XP cylinder gasket seals the cylinder to the crankcase on Husqvarna's big-bore saw. Fit a new one every time the cylinder comes off, whether for a piston and rings or an inspection.

p: A 395XP runs hot and hard, often on the biggest logs of the job. Any air leak at the cylinder base leans the mixture and can cook the piston. A fresh gasket is the cheapest part of the rebuild and one of the most important.
Order it with your other top-end parts from our power equipment parts.
Clean the surfaces gently, set the gasket as the service manual directs, and torque cylinder bolts evenly to spec.
Find the cause of the failure before you run it again. Dirty filters, air leaks at the intake, and poor fuel are the usual suspects. A pressure and vacuum test confirms the seal.

faq.q: Do I need a new gasket if I only lift the cylinder to look?
faq.a: Yes. Once disturbed, the old gasket may not seal again.

faq.q: Is the 395XP gasket the same as the 390XP?
faq.a: Don't assume. Check the part number for your saw.

name: Husqvarna Fuel Hose for 562XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 562XP Fuel Hose Replacement
meta: A replacement Husqvarna 562XP fuel hose for a saw that won't start, dies under load, or leaks fuel. Why fuel line wears out and how to route the new one right.
tagline: A replacement fuel hose for the Husqvarna 562XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 562XP fuel hose replaces a cracked, hardened, or leaking fuel line on the 562XP. A bad fuel hose can let the saw suck air, starve under load, or leak fuel onto a hot engine.
highlights: Fixes fuel leaks and air leaks

body.h: Signs of a bad fuel line
p: Fuel lines age from heat and ethanol. Look for a hose that is stiff, cracked, swollen, or wet at the connections. Symptoms include hard starting, bogging when you open the throttle, and the smell of fuel around the saw.
Replace the fuel filter at the same time. More 562XP parts are in our power equipment parts.
Drain the tank, work with the saw cool and away from ignition sources, and route the new hose exactly as the original ran so it does not rub or kink.
Use ethanol-free or pre-mixed fuel where you can, and don't leave fuel sitting in the saw for months.

faq.q: Why does my 562XP bog when I throttle up?
faq.a: A leaking or collapsed fuel hose, a clogged fuel filter, or an air leak are common causes. Check the fuel system first.

faq.q: Should I replace the fuel filter too?
faq.a: Yes. It's cheap and usually due if the hose is.

name: Husqvarna Inlet Pipe for 395XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 395XP Inlet Pipe (Intake Boot)
meta: A replacement Husqvarna 395XP intake boot, also called the inlet pipe, that joins carburetor and cylinder. A cracked boot causes air leaks and lean seizures.
tagline: A replacement inlet pipe, or intake boot, for the Husqvarna 395XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 395XP intake boot, listed as the inlet pipe, connects the carburetor to the cylinder. When the rubber cracks or hardens, the saw pulls in extra air, runs lean, and risks scoring the piston.
highlights: Common wear item on older saws

p: Heat, age, and fuel break down the rubber over time. A cracked boot is hard to spot from the outside but shows up as a high, hanging idle, erratic running, or a saw that needs the carburetor richened to run. Left alone, it can lead to a lean seizure.
If the boot is bad, check the impulse line too. Both are in our power equipment parts.
Follow the service manual for removing the carburetor and seating the new boot. It must sit fully on both the carb and the cylinder with no twist.
A vacuum test after installation confirms the seal. Then retune the carburetor, since an air leak may have hidden a lean setting.

faq.q: Is the inlet pipe the same as the intake boot?
faq.a: Yes. Husqvarna calls it the inlet pipe; many techs call it the intake boot or manifold.

faq.q: How do I test for an air leak?
faq.a: Use a pressure and vacuum tester on the sealed engine.

name: Husqvarna Seal for 372XP X-Torque
title: Husqvarna 372XP X-Torque Seal Replacement
meta: A replacement Husqvarna 372XP seal for the X-Torque model. Worn seals let air or oil past and cause lean running and leaks. Check the part position before buying.
tagline: A replacement seal for the Husqvarna 372XP X-Torque.
summary: This Husqvarna 372XP seal is a replacement part for the X-Torque version of the 372XP. Seals keep air, fuel, and oil where they belong, and a worn one can cause lean running or leaks.
highlights: Replaces a worn or leaking seal

p: A saw uses several seals, and the most common ones are crankshaft seals on each side of the engine. Check the Husqvarna parts diagram for your model and serial to be sure this is the seal for the position you are replacing.
Browse more 372XP parts in our power equipment parts.
A leaking crank seal often shows up as a high or erratic idle that won't tune out, or fuel residue around the flywheel or clutch side. A pressure and vacuum test pinpoints it.
Install seals square, without nicking the lip, and with the right tool. A damaged lip will leak from the start.

faq.q: Which seal is this?
faq.a: Check the parts diagram for your 372XP X-Torque to match the position before ordering.

faq.q: Can a bad seal ruin my saw?
faq.a: Yes. An air leak makes the saw run lean, which can score the piston and cylinder.

name: Husqvarna Seal for T540XP Top Handle Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna T540XP Top Handle Saw Seal Replacement
h1: Husqvarna Seal for T540XP Top Handle Chainsaw
meta: A replacement Husqvarna T540XP seal for the top-handle climbing saw. Keep the engine sealed so it idles and runs right. Match the seal position before you order.
tagline: A replacement seal for the Husqvarna T540XP top-handle saw.
summary: This Husqvarna T540XP seal is a replacement part for Husqvarna's top-handle climbing saw. A worn seal lets air or oil past, and on a saw you depend on in the tree, a steady idle and clean running matter.
highlights: Replaces a worn or leaking seal
Small part, big difference in reliability

p: When you're tied in at the top of a tree, a saw that won't idle, dies on you, or creeps the chain is more than a nuisance. Seal leaks are one cause of an unstable idle. Confirm which seal your saw needs using the Husqvarna parts diagram for your model and serial.
Find more top-handle parts in our power equipment parts.
Use the correct tools to remove and seat seals without damaging the lip or the crankshaft. Pressure and vacuum test the engine after the repair.
Top-handle saws are for trained arborists working in trees. Follow the operator's manual and ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Why does my T540XP idle high?
faq.a: An air leak through a seal, an intake leak, or the carburetor setting can all cause it. Test before you replace parts.

faq.q: Is this seal also for the T540i XP?
faq.a: No. The T540i XP is the battery version. This part is for the gas T540XP; confirm with the parts list.

name: Husqvarna Starter Spring for Starter Pawl
title: Husqvarna Starter Pawl Spring Replacement
h1: Husqvarna Starter Spring for Starter Pawl
meta: A Husqvarna starter pawl spring that keeps the starter pawls snapping into the flywheel. Fixes a pull cord that spins freely without catching on many models.
tagline: A small spring that returns the starter pawl on Husqvarna saws.
summary: This Husqvarna starter pawl spring holds the starter pawl in position so it catches when you pull the cord and retracts once the engine fires. A broken or weak spring is a common reason a pull cord spins without turning the engine.
highlights: Fixes a starter that won't catch
Fits many Husqvarna saws (check your model)

p: If the starter rope pulls out but the engine doesn't turn, the pawls on the flywheel side are not engaging. Often a pawl spring has broken or lost tension, or a pawl is worn. A quick inspection usually shows the problem.
Check the pawls and the bolt while you're there. Find related starter parts in our power equipment parts.
Confirm this spring matches your saw's model using the Husqvarna parts diagram. Disconnect the spark plug lead before working near the flywheel.
Clean sawdust out of the flywheel area while it's open; packed debris can also keep pawls from moving freely.

faq.q: Will it fit my saw?
faq.a: Many Husqvarna saws share pawl parts, but confirm with the parts diagram for your model.

faq.q: Is this the recoil spring?
faq.a: No. The recoil spring is the large coiled spring in the starter housing. This is the small pawl spring.

name: Husqvarna Washer for 395XP Front Anti-Vibration Mount
title: Husqvarna 395XP Front Anti-Vibration Mount Washer
h1: Husqvarna Washer for 395XP Front Anti-Vibration Mount
meta: A replacement Husqvarna 395XP anti vibration washer for the front AV mount. Keeps the spring seated and the handle tight. Swap it when you replace AV springs.
tagline: A replacement washer for the front anti-vibration mount on the Husqvarna 395XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 395XP anti vibration washer is part of the front AV mount that holds the spring between the handle and the engine. A lost or worn washer can let the spring shift and the handle loosen.
highlights: Helps restore a tight, quiet handle

p: On a heavy saw like the 395XP, the anti-vibration system takes a lot of load. If the washer goes missing during a repair or wears through, the spring can work loose, the handle rattles, and vibration increases.
It's smart to replace washers with the springs. Find springs and other parts in our power equipment parts.
Use the parts diagram to confirm the position and the order of the washer, spring, and screw. Tighten fasteners to spec.
After the repair, check the handle for slop before running the saw, and inspect the other AV mounts at the same time.

faq.q: Do I need this washer if I'm replacing the spring?
faq.a: If the old washer is worn or missing, yes. It keeps the spring seated.

faq.q: Is this for the rear mounts too?
faq.a: This listing is for the front mount. Check the diagram for other positions.

name: Greenteeth 1100 Series WearSharp Teeth
title: Greenteeth 1100 Series WearSharp Stump Grinder Teeth
meta: Greenteeth 1100 series WearSharp teeth for stump grinders running the Greenteeth 1100 pocket system. What sets them apart, and how to rotate and inspect them.
tagline: Carbide stump grinder teeth for the Greenteeth 1100 series pocket system.
summary: Greenteeth 1100 series WearSharp teeth are carbide-tipped stump grinder teeth for wheels set up with the Greenteeth 1100 pocket system. The WearSharp design is meant to keep a cutting edge as the carbide wears, so the grinder keeps cutting instead of rubbing.
highlights: For the Greenteeth 1100 series pocket system
Can be rotated in the pocket for longer life

p: Dull stump grinder teeth slow production, burn fuel, and beat up the machine. Sharp teeth take bigger, cleaner bites. Rocks and dirt are the main enemy, so clear around the stump first.
Match the teeth to the 1100 series pockets on your wheel. See bolts and other parts in our stump grinding section.
Greenteeth are designed to be rotated in the pocket to bring a fresh edge into play. Check teeth, pockets, and bolts every day, and replace any tooth with broken carbide.
Shut the grinder down and wait for the wheel to stop before touching it. Keep people and vehicles well back, use guards and debris shields, and wear eye, face, and hearing protection.

faq.q: Will these fit my wheel?
faq.a: Only if it uses the Greenteeth 1100 series pocket system. Check your wheel.

faq.q: Do I rotate or replace them?
faq.a: Rotate them to use other edges, and replace when the carbide is broken or worn out.

name: Greenteeth Stump Grinder Bolt
title: Greenteeth Stump Grinder Bolt Replacement
meta: A replacement Greenteeth stump grinder bolt for holding pockets and teeth on the cutter wheel. Why worn bolts are a hazard and how to check them every day.
tagline: A replacement bolt for Greenteeth pockets and teeth on a stump grinder wheel.
summary: This Greenteeth stump grinder bolt secures the teeth and pockets on a Greenteeth cutter wheel. Bolts take a beating from rocks and vibration, and a worn or stretched one can let a tooth come loose.
highlights: Secures teeth and pockets to the wheel
Replace worn or damaged bolts promptly

p: The wheel on a stump grinder spins fast and hits wood, dirt, and stones. A tooth thrown from the wheel is dangerous. Bolts with worn heads, damaged threads, or signs of stretching should be replaced, not reused.
Match bolts to your Greenteeth series. More teeth and parts are in our stump grinding section.
With the machine off and the wheel stopped, inspect bolts and nuts and torque them to Green Manufacturing's spec. Check again after hitting a rock.
Keep the work area clear, use the grinder's guards and a debris shield, and wear eye, face, and hearing protection.

faq.q: Can I reuse old bolts?
faq.a: Replace any bolt that is worn, bent, or damaged. Follow Green Manufacturing's guidance on replacement.

faq.q: How tight should they be?
faq.a: Use the torque spec from Green Manufacturing for your system.

name: Stein Modular Guard System Replacement Panel
title: Stein Modular Guard System Replacement Panel
h1: Stein Modular Guard System Replacement Panel
meta: A replacement panel for the Stein modular guard system, a portable debris screen for stump grinding. Replace damaged panels to keep chips and stones contained.
tagline: A replacement screen panel for Stein's portable stump grinding guard.
summary: This replacement panel fits the Stein modular guard system, a portable screen set up around a stump grinding job to help contain flying chips and stones. Replace a damaged panel to keep the barrier complete.
highlights: Replacement panel for the Stein modular guard
Helps contain debris from stump grinding
Swap out a damaged panel without replacing the set

p: Stump grinders throw chips, dirt, and stones a long way. Near houses, cars, windows, and sidewalks, a portable guard set up around the stump adds a barrier on top of the machine's own guards.
A modular system lets you shape the screen to the job and replace one panel when it gets damaged. See more in our stump grinding section.
Set panels on the side where people, property, or traffic are at risk, and keep the screen stable. Inspect panels for tears, holes, or bent frames, and replace any that are damaged.
A guard does not replace an exclusion zone. Keep bystanders clear, and wear eye, face, and hearing protection when grinding.

faq.q: Can I buy one panel instead of a full set?
faq.a: Yes. This listing is a single replacement panel for an existing Stein system.

faq.q: Does a guard mean bystanders can stand close?
faq.a: No. Keep a clear zone around the grinder at all times.
